n: The Lord addresses high priests gathered in Kirtland in March 1832. When first printed, some names in this revelation were replaced with code names to protect the Church’s business affairs.
He counsels them with wisdom concerning the matter they have brought before him.
The time has come to organize the storehouse for the poor in Kirtland and Zion. This led to the “United Firm,” which managed the Church’s storehouses and publishing.
It is to be a permanent order advancing the cause of salvation and glorifying the Father.
The goal: to be equal in heavenly and earthly things, for the sake of gaining heavenly things.

f.w: equal in the bonds of heavenly things

n: If they aren’t equal in earthly things, they can’t be equal in heavenly things. How we share material things shapes our spiritual readiness.

f.w: if ye are not equal in earthly things

n: To gain a place in the celestial world, they must prepare by obeying his commands.

f.w: a place in the celestial world

n: All should be done for God’s glory by those joined in this order.
Newel K. Whitney, Joseph Smith, and Sidney Rigdon are to go to Missouri and counsel with the Saints there. They traveled to Missouri in April 1832.
Otherwise Satan will turn the Missouri Saints’ hearts away, blinding them to what is prepared for them. Tensions had grown between leaders in Ohio and Missouri.
They must organize by an everlasting covenant that cannot be broken.
Whoever breaks it loses office and standing and is delivered to the “buffetings of Satan” until redemption—left without God’s protection to experience the adversary’s attacks.
This is the preparation, foundation, and example to help them keep his commands.
Through God’s care, despite coming hardships, the Church may stand independent of all other powers under heaven. Self-reliance is a spiritual principle.
So they may receive their crown and rule over many kingdoms. The Lord is the Holy One of Zion, who established Adam-ondi-Ahman.

f.g: The place where Adam blessed his posterity; later identified with a site in Daviess County, Missouri.

n: He appointed Michael—Adam—as their prince and gave him the keys of salvation under the direction of the Holy One, who has no beginning or end.

f.w: without beginning of days or end of life

n: They are still little children who don’t yet understand the blessings the Father has prepared.
They can’t bear everything now, but be of good cheer—he will lead them along. The kingdom and eternity’s riches are theirs.
Whoever receives all things with thankfulness will be made glorious, and earthly blessings will be added a hundredfold. Gratitude itself is a path to glory.
Obey, says the Redeemer, the “Son Ahman,” who prepares all things. “Ahman” was revealed as a name for God, making “Son Ahman” a title of Christ.

f.g: A title for Jesus Christ; Ahman is given as a name of God the Father.

n: They are the Church of the Firstborn; he will take them up in a cloud and appoint each person his portion.

f.w: take you up in a cloud

n: The faithful and wise steward will inherit all things.
